A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and are readable throughout. v2 ends at the references, with an in-text proof sketch despite referring to an absent Appendix A; v3 includes Appendices A–E. The retained text, equations, tables, and figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original classification results on four point-cloud datasets, cross-architecture evaluations, training times, and component ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds cross-dataset evaluations, controlled comparisons, additional baseline results, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions use channel-wise feature sorting, Gaussian-kernel distribution matching with an additional top-feature loss, and joint optimization of synthetic coordinates and rotation angles. v3 adds explicit notation and implementation details without establishing a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The four classification datasets remain ModelNet10, ModelNet40, ShapeNet, and ScanObjectNN. v3 adds reciprocal transfer between ModelNet40 and ShapeNet using their 16 shared classes (Section 4.2.3), extending test scenarios within the retained domains. Appendix B's identification of the ScanObjectNN split is newly disclosed detail, not evidence of added coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated MTT and DataDAM baselines across all four datasets and three PPC values (Table 13), substantially broadening the distillation comparison. It also compares axis-aligned and Z-order sorting (Table 9) and random rotation augmentation (Table 14). Existing comparators remain, including PCC as DC with Herding initialization.

E3.justification: The original 1,500-iteration, 1,024-point, PPC 1/3/10 evaluation remains unchanged. Added experiments introduce targeted protocols: reciprocal transfer over 16 shared classes, equal training time against DM, sorting comparisons with rotation optimization disabled, and random rotation augmentation. Newly documented architecture and optimizer settings do not establish revisions to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained semantic-alignment and rotation ablations, v3 tests spatial sorting alternatives, rotation augmentation, cross-dataset transfer, and performance under equal training time. Appendix E adds analyses of optimization from noise and diversity across PPC values (Figures 9–10), substantially extending evidence about mechanisms and robustness.

E5.justification: Both versions state that evaluation networks are trained 10 times and report mean accuracy and standard deviation; the corresponding tables retain those values. Added tables use point estimates, a practice already present in v2. No new seed information, uncertainty estimation procedure, confidence interval, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: All six original result tables retain their values after renumbering. v3 adds substantial results in Tables 3, 6, 9, 13, and 14 and qualitative findings in Appendix E. For example, the new equal-time comparison reports 83.64 for the proposed method versus 77.58 for DM on ModelNet10 at PPC 3; this is new controlled evidence, not a performance gain over v2.

T1.justification: The joint-optimization inequality and its feasible-set reasoning are unchanged. v3's expanded feature matrix, explicit joint objective, and Appendix A formalize mathematics already expressed in v2's definitions and proof sketch, without adding an assumption, theoretical result, or new proof argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: distribution-matching distillation for 3D point clouds using SADM and joint rotation optimization, with superior classification and cross-architecture generalization. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v3 interprets cross-dataset transfer as evidence of reusable geometric patterns and explains spatial sorting's weakness through inconsistent semantic alignment. Appendix D attributes augmentation-related degradation on aligned datasets to unnecessary rotational variation. These extend the interpretation while the substantive limitations in Section 4.4 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies extensive information absent from v2: train/test counts, the PB_T50_RS split, architecture variants, optimizer settings, PPC-dependent loss weights, rotation learning rates, evaluation schedules, GPU hardware, and baseline configurations (Tables 10–12). These disclosures substantially improve reproducibility without establishing that the retained experiments changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Morton's 1966 work for Z-order sorting; the other cited works are retained. Section 2 more explicitly connects the reviewed architectures and coreset limitations to this work. MTT and DataDAM were already cited in v2, although their empirical evaluation is new.

P1.justification: v3 polishes the abstract and selected introduction, experimental, and conclusion paragraphs, condenses Section 2.1, and clarifies mathematical notation. It adds supplementary sections and acknowledgements and updates the conference header, while retaining the main narrative and section order.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the displays with new comparison tables, dataset and hyperparameter tables, and Figures 4–12 covering baseline outputs, class galleries, convergence, and PPC diversity. Existing tables are rearranged and renumbered, Figure 3 is relocated, and Table 1's caption explains 'Whole' and 'Ratio'; the original result displays remain substantively intact.

improvement.justification: Appendix B resolves substantial gaps in reproducibility, while the additional baselines, equal-time control, and sorting, augmentation, and transfer tests strengthen evaluation of the central claims. These are substantive gains beyond added volume. v3 introduces an unexplained reporting inconsistency—Table 13 gives 84.96 for ModelNet10 at PPC 3 while retained Table 1 gives 84.4—but this limited issue does not outweigh the improvements in documentation and experimental support.
